title: DOJ Issues Subpoenas in Alaska Senate Race Over Alleged 'Dan Sullivan' Ballot Scheme
snippet: Federal prosecutors are ramping up a criminal probe into an alleged Democratic plot to recruit a second candidate named Dan Sullivan to confuse Alaska voters.
content:
The Justice Department has escalated its criminal investigation into Alaska's high-stakes U.S. Senate race, issuing a new wave of subpoenas aimed at Democratic officials involved in an alleged recruitment scheme to place a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.

The federal probe centers on whether allies of Democratic candidate Mary Peltola coordinated an effort to put Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher, on the ballot to siphon votes away from the incumbent Republican senator, Dan Sullivan. While no individuals have been charged with a crime, federal authorities are scrutinizing internal emails and text messages detailed in recent reporting to determine if election laws were violated.

Federal Investigators Eye Civil Rights Charges

During a briefing with reporters, Justice Department officials revealed a "significant increase in activity" surrounding the case, indicating prosecutors are exploring potential violations of federal civil rights statutes. Specifically, authorities are pointing to 18 U.S.C. Sections 241 and 242—laws that prohibit conspiracies to interfere with constitutional rights, including the right to vote.

Officials suggested the alleged tactic resembles a coordinated attempt to deceive voters at the ballot box, drawing parallels to previous federal prosecutions involving deceptive campaign tactics. To expand the probe, investigators may utilize grand jury subpoenas, search warrants for electronic records, and formal preservation requests sent to tech companies.

Despite the intensifying criminal inquiry, DOJ officials acknowledged they have not yet confirmed any instances where an Alaska voter mistakenly cast a ballot for the wrong Dan Sullivan.

Legal and State-Level Fallout Grows

The criminal investigation coincides with a civil lawsuit brought by the Trump administration aimed at preventing Alaska from certifying the Senate election results if the Republican incumbent loses due to voter confusion. The lawsuit was recently amended to characterize the alleged recruitment operation as a "conspiracy to undermine the integrity of the electoral process."

President Donald Trump took direct credit for initiating the civil action, telling reporters, "I'm the one that said, 'Do it.'" Meanwhile, Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy has directed Alaska's Department of Public Safety to conduct a parallel state investigation to determine if state election laws were broken.

Both the Peltola campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee have forcefully denied any involvement in placing Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot. For his part, the retired teacher has maintained that his candidacy was driven by a genuine interest in public service.
